Video Studio: a still image becomes a video, from inside the console. @hl-bos/video-studio finds the panels in a composite image by scoring every row and column for uniformity (a gutter is uniform along its length, artwork is not), plans a shot list of pans and zooms, and resolves that plan to exact rectangles at any millisecond; the Control Center's /video page records it to a real .mp4 in the browser with no account, no key and no upload. Verified end to end in headless Chromium against the CEO's own six-panel image: 6 panels found in a 3x2 grid, 8 shots, 16.7s, 1440x1416 MP4 of 7.3 MB that decodes and contains real frames. 62 unit tests. One real defect was found and fixed by that verification: the first cut cropped near-square comic panels to 16:9 and deleted the artist's caption bars, and the fix (contain-by-default framing) exposed a second bug where the renderer stretched instead of padding -- both now have regression tests that fail without the fix. Generated motion (a video model that animates the picture) is NOT built: the page names it, says what it would take, and shows no button for it.

blockers.meaning: Deploying needs a preview environment to test against, and Supabase branching is not switched on. Building a Deploy button before then would be a button that cannot deploy.

blockers.title: Social channels are not connected yet
blockers.meaning: The publishing software is built and tested, but it has no accounts to publish to. Six things are needed before the first real post: the exact list of Facebook Pages, Instagram accounts, LinkedIn profile and TikTok accounts to use; confirmation each Instagram account is a Professional account linked to a Facebook Page (a personal account cannot post automatically at all); a Meta app with the Instagram and Facebook Login products; a tester/admin role on that app for each account; a LinkedIn app with 'Share on LinkedIn'; and a TikTok app with inbox-only content posting. Each is an access decision only you can make. Everything not waiting on them is finished.

blockers.title: Production has drifted from the repository, and the safe apply path is blocked
blockers.meaning: While applying the social migration I checked what the live database actually contains. It holds about forty migrations that are not in this repository at all (three separate naming schemes: dma_*, disco_*, jobscout_*), and around fourteen of our own migrations were applied under different version stamps than the files carry. The registry file that is supposed to track this still says the database is at migration 28; it is far past that. The practical consequence: the protected one-click migration workflow cannot be used safely right now -- its drift check would fail, and if it were forced past that it would try to re-run around twenty migrations the database already has under other names, including two data backfills. That is why 0046 and 0047 were applied individually and verified rather than pushed as a batch. Reconciling this properly is its own piece of work and needs your go-ahead; it is not urgent, but it should not be left indefinitely.
